title: Recording a country single with Mac Wiseman
summary: Herman recorded My Blue Heaven and If I Could Be With You with bluegrass figure Mac Wiseman, on a friend's small country label.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, and when I was there, I decided -- a friend of mine has a small country label, and we decided we'd do a single. And I recorded a couple of very, very old songs with a legendary figure down in Nashville by the name of Mac Wiseman, who's a very strong influence and has been for many years in the bluegrass field.
How do you spell his name?
And we did an old tune that was first introduced a hundred years ago by Gene Austin, called My Blue Heaven. // //
And then we took an old tune that you will remember because it was done a lot by jazz people. // If I Could Be With You One Hour Tonight. // And found out that Harry
Berenson in the late '20s, wrote a song to be sung or played as an obligato against that tune, called It Must Be True.

And so we did the oldest gimmick in the world, (inaudible) which is, the last half of the last chorus. One sings one tune and the other sings the other tune. And we had what they call in Nashville circles housewives' disco beat. Which Threw me a curve.
Was this some singles or some --
Yeah, just -- we did this as a single recording, which should be out any time. I'm waiting for the final mix. The producer is a very consistent guy down there who's had much success.
I don't know my friend's label. I have to find out, but it's -- but he's had some pretty good showing on the charts in the country field.
And so it'll be Herman and Wiseman or Wiseman and Herman or something like that.
